o: Elimelech and his sons die in the land of Moab.
Orpah stays behind, but Ruth goes with Naomi.
bg: ruth, book of

contains the history of Ruth, as narrated in the preceding article. The main object of the writer is evidently to give an account of David's ancestors; and the book was avowedly composed long after the time of the heroine.
Naomi
or Nao'mi (my delight), the wife of Elimelech and mother-in-law of Ruth. (Ruth 1:2) etc.; Ruth 2:1 etc.; Ruth 3:1; 4:3 etc.
Moab

The land of Moab (Jer. 48:24), called also the "country of Moab" (Ruth 1:2, 6; 2:6), on the east of Jordan and the Dead Sea, and south of the Arnon (Num. 21:13, 26). In a wider sense it included the whole region that had been occupied by the Amorites.
Ruth

A friend, a Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, whose father, Elimelech, had settled in the land of Moab. On the death of Elimelech and Mahlon, Naomi came with Ruth, her daughter-in-law, who refused to leave her, to Bethlehem, the old home from which Elimelech had migrated.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Elimelech and his sons die in the land of Moab (vv. 1–5); Naomi returns home (vv. 6–14); Orpah stays behind, but Ruth goes with Naomi (vv. 15–18); They come to Bethlehem (vv. 19–22). People named: Naomi, Moab, Ruth, Elimelech, Chilion, Orpah. Places: Judah.
ch.mh: Elimelech's care to provide for his family, was not to be blamed; but his removal into the country of Moab could not be justified.
q: Read verses 1–5 (Elimelech and his sons die in the land of Moab). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 6–14 (Naomi returns home), what do you learn about family and generations?
Verse 16 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside 2 Samuel 15:21. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Naomi’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of hope and restoration in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Ruth?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: It is folly to think of escaping that cross, which, being laid in our way, we ought to take up.
ch.a: Encourage someone who is discouraged with a promise from this chapter.

q: Read verses 1–3 (Ruth gleans in the field of Boaz). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 4–16 (The kindness of Boaz to Ruth), what do you learn about family and generations?
Verse 12 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Psalms 36:7. How do the two passages shed light on each other?

ch.aq: When the Lord deals bountifully with us, let us not be found in any other field, nor seeking for happiness and satisfaction in the creature.
ch.a: Before a decision this week, pause and ask what this chapter would counsel.
